market_context: U.S. futures were modestly positive after Monday’s sharp decline, with S&P 500 futures up about 0.2% and Nasdaq 100 futures up about 0.3% as oil prices and Treasury yields eased.[1] However, the 10-year yield remained near 5.22%-5.28%, close to multi-year highs, while geopolitical uncertainty and expectations for another Federal Reserve rate hike continue to limit risk appetite.[2][8] The main scheduled U.S. data point identified was the Redbook retail-sales reading, reported at 7.6% year over year.[10][11]

predictions.reasoning: S&P 500 futures were approximately 0.2% higher before the open after Monday’s 0.8% cash-market decline, while easing oil prices and a small pullback in Treasury yields provided a modest relief signal.[1][5] The elevated 10-year yield near 5.2% makes a large rebound unlikely, so the forecast targets a limited recovery of roughly 0.4%.

Nasdaq 100 futures gained about 0.3% as yields retreated from their intraday peak, offering some support to rate-sensitive technology shares.[1][5] Persistent high real borrowing costs and AI-related investor jitters argue for a smaller move than a full reversal of Monday’s decline.

Although Nasdaq futures were modestly higher, technology sentiment remained vulnerable to elevated Treasury yields and reported AI-related jitters.[1][9] Nvidia’s high duration and valuation sensitivity make it more exposed than the broad market if yields resume their rise during the session.

The broader market was attempting only a limited stabilization after Monday’s selloff, while elevated yields and geopolitical uncertainty remained headwinds for high-beta growth stocks.[2][3] Tesla’s volatility makes a modest underperformance plausible even if index futures remain slightly positive.
